question:
Select the word that has the same meaning (SYNONYM) as the underlined word in the given sentence.

She accused her sister of being vindictive when she was trying to defame her.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. revengeful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Vindictive" means having a strong desire for revenge; spiteful. (प्रतिशोधी / बदला लेने वाला)

◦ Example: His vindictive remarks were meant to hurt her.

• Its closest synonym is "revengeful" — eager to take revenge.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 — Vigilant: watchful and alert to danger.

• Option 3 — Righteous: morally right or justifiable.

• Option 4 — Venerable: deserving great respect due to age or dignity.

NOTE

• Synonyms of vindictive: vengeful, spiteful, malicious, resentful. Antonyms: forgiving, merciful, magnanimous.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

My grandparents live in a beautiful house __________ the countryside.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. in.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "in" is used with large areas / broad locations such as the countryside, cities, and regions. Hence "in the countryside". (के ग्रामीण इलाके में)

◦ Example: They spent their holidays in the mountains.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 — "on" is used for surfaces (on the table) and lines (on the road).

• Option 3 — "onto" shows movement towards a surface (jumped onto the bed).

• Option 4 — "at" is used for specific points/places (at the bus stop).

NOTE

• Prepositions of place: in (enclosed/large areas), on (surfaces), at (specific points). "In the countryside" is a fixed expression.

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

The children were merry than usual on Sunday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. merrier.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" signals a comparison between two situations, so the comparative degree is required. The comparative of "merry" is "merrier".

◦ Correct: The children were merrier than usual on Sunday.

• Adjectives ending in "-y" form the comparative by changing "y" to "i" and adding "-er" (merry → merrier).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 — "more merrier" is a double comparative (both "more" and "-er"), which is wrong.

• Options 2 and 3 — "the merriest / merriest" are superlative forms, used for three or more, not with "than".

NOTE

• Degrees: merry (positive) – merrier (comparative, with "than") – merriest (superlative, with "the"). Never combine "more" with an "-er" form.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

They looked out the matter and found the root cause of the problem.
option_1: looked of the matter and found
option_2: looked until the matter and found
option_3: looked unless the matter and found
option_4: looked into the matter and found
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. looked into the matter and found.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "look into" means to investigate or examine (a matter). It fits the context of finding the root cause of a problem. (जाँच करना)

◦ Example: The police will look into the complaint.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "looked of" is not a valid phrasal verb.

• Option 2 "looked until" and Option 3 "looked unless" use conjunctions of time/condition, which are meaningless here.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "look": look into (investigate), look after (take care of), look for (search), look up to (respect), look down on (despise).

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in future tense form.

Since next Friday, the team of three members has been tracking the animal.
option_1: From next Friday, the team of three members are tracking the animal.
option_2: Since last Friday, the team of three members had tracked the animal.
option_3: From next Friday, the team of three members have been tracking the animal.
option_4: From next Friday, the team of three members will be tracking the animal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. From next Friday, the team of three members will be tracking the animal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To express a future action, the future continuous tense (will be + V-ing) is appropriate: "will be tracking". Also, "From next Friday" correctly indicates a future starting point.

◦ Example: From tomorrow, I will be working on the new project.

• The subject "the team" is singular, so "will be" agrees correctly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 uses present continuous ("are tracking") and a plural verb — not future and not agreeing with "team".

• Option 2 is in the past perfect ("had tracked").

• Option 3 uses "have been tracking" (present perfect continuous) and a plural verb.

NOTE

• Future continuous (will be + V-ing) describes an action that will be in progress at a future time. Use "from" (not "since") for future starting points.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word in the given sentence.

The athlete demonstrated remarkable agility during the gymnastics routine.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Stiffness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Agility" means the ability to move quickly and easily; nimbleness. (फुर्ती / चपलता)

• Its antonym is "stiffness", which means rigidity or lack of easy movement.

◦ Example: The old hinge moved with great stiffness.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 — Nimbleness and Option 3 — Flexibility are synonyms of agility.

• Option 2 — Prowess means skill or expertise, not opposite in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of agility: nimbleness, suppleness, dexterity, quickness. Antonyms: stiffness, clumsiness, sluggishness.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Apple of one's eye
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Very precious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "apple of one's eye" refers to a person (or thing) that is cherished above all others; someone very precious/dear. (आँखों का तारा)

◦ Example: His youngest daughter is the apple of his eye.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 4 — "very docile", "very strong" and "very stubborn" do not convey the sense of being dearly loved.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of affection/value: to hold someone dear, to think the world of someone, one's pride and joy.

question: Select the sentence with the most appropriate use of preposition.
option_1: Reetu slept all in the history class.
option_2: Reetu slept all through the history class.
option_3: Reetu slept all during the history class.
option_4: Reetu slept all into the history class.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Reetu slept all through the history class.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "through" is used to mean from the beginning to the end of a period — "all through the class" = for the entire duration of the class. (पूरे समय)

◦ Example: She stayed awake all through the night.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "all in" and Option 4 "all into" are not correct prepositional usages here.

• Option 3 "all during" is incorrect; "during" is not used with "all" in this way.

NOTE

• "Through" indicates movement from start to finish of a time span. Compare: throughout the day, all through the year.

question:
Read the sentence given below and identify if there is an error in it. The error can be in any segment of the sentence which are marked A, B, C, and D. Select option D if there is 'No error'.

(A) Ritika angrily / (B) spoke to Kartik / (C) after the meeting / (D) No error.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. D (No error).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Ritika angrily spoke to Kartik after the meeting" is grammatically correct. The adverb "angrily" is correctly placed before the verb "spoke", and the prepositions and word order are all proper.

◦ Example: She quietly closed the door after the class.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 (segment D — No error).

Additional Information

• Segment A ("Ritika angrily") — correct; adverbs of manner can precede the main verb.

• Segment B ("spoke to Kartik") — correct use of "spoke to".

• Segment C ("after the meeting") — correct prepositional phrase of time.

NOTE

• Adverbs of manner (angrily, quickly, softly) usually come before the main verb or after the object — both positions are acceptable.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Blunt
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Insensitive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Blunt", when describing a person or speech, means direct and outspoken to the point of being rude or insensitive. (मुँहफट / बेलाग)

◦ Example: His blunt reply hurt her feelings.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 — Adventurous: willing to take risks (unrelated).

• Option 3 — Tactful: careful not to offend — the antonym of blunt.

• Option 4 — Rowdy: noisy and disorderly (unrelated).

NOTE

• "Blunt" also means "not sharp" (a blunt knife). As a personality trait: blunt = frank, curt, brusque, insensitive.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The children's laughter was filled with exuberant joy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. repressed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Exuberant" means full of energy, excitement and cheerfulness; unrestrained. (उत्साहपूर्ण / उमंग भरा)

• Its antonym is "repressed", meaning restrained, held back or subdued.

◦ Example: His repressed anger finally burst out.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 — Flawless: perfect, without faults (unrelated).

• Option 2 — Euphoric: intensely happy — a synonym, not antonym.

• Option 3 — Sarcastic: using irony to mock (unrelated).

NOTE

• Synonyms of exuberant: lively, ebullient, effervescent, high-spirited. Antonyms: repressed, subdued, lethargic, dull.

question:
Change the following sentence into superlative degree.

No other mountain in the world is as high as the Mount Everest.
option_1: No other mountain is highest than Mount Everest.
option_2: Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
option_3: Mount Everest is higher than any other mountain in the world.
option_4: Mount Everest is high mountain in the world.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The pattern "No other ... is as high as X" (positive degree) is equivalent, in the superlative degree, to "X is the highest ...".

◦ Rule: No other + noun + as + adjective + as + X → X is the + superlative adjective + noun.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "highest than" wrongly mixes the superlative with "than".

• Option 3 "higher than any other" is the comparative degree form (also correct in sense, but not superlative).

• Option 4 omits the article/superlative and is grammatically incomplete.

NOTE

• Interchange of degrees: Positive – "No other X is as tall as A"; Comparative – "A is taller than any other X"; Superlative – "A is the tallest X".

question:
One of the four words in bold in the given sentence is incorrectly spelt. Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.

The hurricane left behind a devasstating trail of destruction.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. devasstating.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Devasstating" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "devastating" (with a single "s"), meaning highly destructive or damaging. (विनाशकारी)

◦ Example: The flood had a devastating effect on the village.

• Spelling key: DE + VAS + TAT + ING (only one "s").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Trail", "hurricane" and "destruction" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related forms: devastate (verb), devastation (noun), devastating (adjective), devastated (past/adjective).

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The farm cattle is grazing in the field when the tiger attacked.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. is grazing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subordinate clause "when the tiger attacked" is in the past tense, so the main verb must also be in the past continuous — "was grazing", not "is grazing".

◦ Correct: The farm cattle was grazing in the field when the tiger attacked.

• "Cattle" here is treated as a unit; the tense error (present vs past) is the key mistake.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "The farm cattle" — acceptable as the subject.

• "in the field when" — correct.

• "the tiger attacked" — correct (simple past for the interrupting action).

NOTE

• Sequence of tenses: an action in progress in the past (was/were + V-ing) is interrupted by a shorter past action (simple past) — "was grazing ... when ... attacked".

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence.

The artist's unique technique added a touch of individiuality to the painting.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Individiuality.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Individiuality" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "individuality", meaning the quality that distinguishes one person or thing from others. (व्यक्तित्व / विशिष्टता)

◦ Example: Her paintings show great individuality.

• Spelling key: IN + DI + VI + DU + AL + I + TY (note "vidu", not "vidiu").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Unique", "Technique" and "Artist's" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related words: individual, individually, individuality, individualism. The "-que" ending (unique, technique, antique) comes from French.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The loud thunder _______ the children, making them cry.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. frightened.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Frightened" means made someone afraid or scared. It logically explains why the children cried on hearing the loud thunder. (डरा दिया)

◦ Example: The sudden noise frightened the baby.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 — Fastened: fixed or tied firmly (unrelated).

• Option 2 — Fainted: lost consciousness; also, the verb here would need "made ... faint", so it does not fit grammatically or in sense.

• Option 4 — Fancied: imagined or desired (unrelated).

NOTE

• Synonyms of frighten: scare, terrify, alarm, startle, spook. Antonyms: reassure, comfort, calm.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

When pigs fly
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Something that will never happen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "when pigs fly" is used to say that something is impossible and will never happen (because pigs cannot fly). (जो कभी नहीं होगा)

◦ Example: "He will clean his room when pigs fly," she said sarcastically.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 3 do not capture the sense of impossibility conveyed by the idiom.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of impossibility: "once in a blue moon" (very rarely), "not in a million years", "when hell freezes over".

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

Placing a huge magnet atop the temple pose to being the biggest hurdle for the masons.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. posed to be.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "Placing a huge magnet atop the temple" is a singular gerund phrase describing a past difficulty, so the correct verb form is "posed to be" (past tense), giving a grammatical sentence.

◦ Correct: Placing a huge magnet atop the temple posed to be the biggest hurdle for the masons.

• The original "pose to being" is grammatically wrong (wrong verb form + "being").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is wrong because the underlined part clearly needs correction.

• Option 2 "posing as be" and Option 3 "poses for being" are both ungrammatical.

NOTE

• "Pose" here means "to present/constitute (a problem or difficulty)": the task posed a challenge / posed to be difficult.

question:
Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Rahul's personality is complamented by his confident looks.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. complemented.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "complemented", from "complement" — meaning to complete or enhance by providing something additional. His confident looks complement (go well with) his personality. (पूरक होना)

◦ Example: The wine perfectly complemented the meal.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Options 1, 2 and 4 ("complamanted", "complimited", "complieminted") are all misspellings and not real words.

NOTE

• Do not confuse complement (to complete/enhance) with compliment (to praise). "Her scarf complements her dress" vs "He complimented her on her dress".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Enmity
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Friendship.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Enmity" means a feeling of active hostility or hatred between people. (शत्रुता / दुश्मनी)

• Its antonym is "friendship", a relationship of mutual affection and goodwill.

◦ Example: Years of enmity finally gave way to friendship.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 — Malignity, Option 2 — Antipathy and Option 3 — Hostility are all synonyms of enmity, not antonyms.

NOTE

• Synonyms of enmity: hostility, animosity, antagonism, antipathy. Antonyms: friendship, amity, goodwill, harmony.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

A monsoon is traditionally a seasonal reversing wind (1)__________ by corresponding changes in precipitation but is now (2)__________ describe seasonal changes in atmospheric circulation and precipitation associated (3)__________ annual latitudinal oscillation of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) between its limits to the north and south of the equator. Usually, the term monsoon (4)__________ refer to the rainy phase of a seasonally changing pattern, although technically there is also a dry phase. The term is also sometimes used to (5)__________ locally heavy but short-term rains.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. accompanied.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank needs a past participle to form a reduced passive clause — "a seasonal reversing wind accompanied by corresponding changes in precipitation". The structure "accompanied by" describes what goes along with the wind. (के साथ)

◦ Example: Thunder is usually accompanied by lightning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "accompanies" and Option 2 "accompany" are finite/base forms that do not fit the passive "... wind ___ by ...".

• Option 4 "accompanying" (present participle) would need a different structure and does not pair with "by" here.

NOTE

• "Accompanied by" is a fixed passive collocation meaning "together with / along with".

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

A monsoon is traditionally a seasonal reversing wind (1)__________ by corresponding changes in precipitation but is now (2)__________ describe seasonal changes in atmospheric circulation and precipitation associated (3)__________ annual latitudinal oscillation of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) between its limits to the north and south of the equator. Usually, the term monsoon (4)__________ refer to the rainy phase of a seasonally changing pattern, although technically there is also a dry phase. The term is also sometimes used to (5)__________ locally heavy but short-term rains.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. used to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "is now used to describe" is the correct passive structure — "the term is used to describe seasonal changes". (के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है)

◦ Example: This tool is used to measure temperature.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "using to" and Option 4 "use to" are grammatically incorrect after "is now".

• Option 3 "uses to" wrongly makes the verb active/singular, clashing with "is now".

NOTE

• "Be used to + base verb" = to be employed for a purpose (is used to describe). Do not confuse with "used to + verb" (a past habit) or "be used to + -ing" (be accustomed to).

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

A monsoon is traditionally a seasonal reversing wind (1)__________ by corresponding changes in precipitation but is now (2)__________ describe seasonal changes in atmospheric circulation and precipitation associated (3)__________ annual latitudinal oscillation of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) between its limits to the north and south of the equator. Usually, the term monsoon (4)__________ refer to the rainy phase of a seasonally changing pattern, although technically there is also a dry phase. The term is also sometimes used to (5)__________ locally heavy but short-term rains.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. with.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The collocation required is "associated with" — meaning connected or linked to. Here the precipitation is "associated with the annual latitudinal oscillation of the ITCZ". (के साथ जुड़ा हुआ)

◦ Example: Smoking is associated with many diseases.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Associated on/for/of" are all incorrect prepositions; the verb "associate" collocates with "with".

NOTE

• Verbs that take "with": associated with, connected with, linked with, coupled with, compared with.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

A monsoon is traditionally a seasonal reversing wind (1)__________ by corresponding changes in precipitation but is now (2)__________ describe seasonal changes in atmospheric circulation and precipitation associated (3)__________ annual latitudinal oscillation of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) between its limits to the north and south of the equator. Usually, the term monsoon (4)__________ refer to the rainy phase of a seasonally changing pattern, although technically there is also a dry phase. The term is also sometimes used to (5)__________ locally heavy but short-term rains.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. is used to.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "the term monsoon" is singular and the statement is a present general fact, so the correct passive form is "is used to refer" — "the term monsoon is used to refer to the rainy phase". (संदर्भित करने के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "is use to" is ungrammatical (needs the past participle "used").

• Option 3 "are used to" uses a plural verb, wrong for the singular subject "the term".

• Option 4 "were used to" is past tense, clashing with the present context ("usually").

NOTE

• "Is used to + base verb" expresses purpose in the present passive: the term is used to refer / describe / denote something.

question:
Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

A monsoon is traditionally a seasonal reversing wind (1)__________ by corresponding changes in precipitation but is now (2)__________ describe seasonal changes in atmospheric circulation and precipitation associated (3)__________ annual latitudinal oscillation of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) between its limits to the north and south of the equator. Usually, the term monsoon (4)__________ refer to the rainy phase of a seasonally changing pattern, although technically there is also a dry phase. The term is also sometimes used to (5)__________ locally heavy but short-term rains.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. describe.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the structure "used to" (be used to + base verb), we need the base form of the verb — "the term is sometimes used to describe locally heavy but short-term rains". (वर्णन करने के लिए)

◦ Example: This word is used to describe a happy mood.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "describes" (singular present) and Option 3 "described" (past participle) do not follow "used to".

• Option 4 "describing" (-ing form) would fit only after "be accustomed to", not "be used to (for a purpose)".

NOTE

• "Be used to + base verb" always takes the base form: used to describe, used to measure, used to denote.

question: As per Article 51A of the Constitution of India, Fundamental Duty (h) is to develop the __________, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
solution_text:
The correct answer is scientific temper.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per Article 51A(h) of the Constitution of India, it is a Fundamental Duty of every citizen "to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform." (वैज्ञानिक दृष्टिकोण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, based on the USSR model.

• Originally 10 duties were listed; the 86th Amendment (2002) added the 11th duty (Article 51A(k)) — a parent/guardian to provide education to children aged 6–14 years.

NOTE

• Fundamental Duties are contained in Part IV-A (Article 51A) of the Constitution and are non-justiciable (not legally enforceable).

question: In which state is Kawal Wildlife Sanctuary located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Telangana.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kawal Wildlife Sanctuary (also a Tiger Reserve) is located in the Jannaram area of Mancherial district, Telangana, on the banks of the Godavari and Kadam rivers. (कवल वन्यजीव अभयारण्य — तेलंगाना)

• It was declared a Tiger Reserve in 2012.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other important protected areas of Telangana: Amrabad Tiger Reserve, Pakhal, Eturnagaram and Kinnerasani wildlife sanctuaries.

NOTE

• Kawal is part of the catchment area of the Godavari river and is rich in dry deciduous teak forests and grasslands.

question: According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021, which Union Territory has the lowest proportion of poor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Puducherry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021, released by NITI Aayog, Puducherry had the lowest proportion of multidimensionally poor people among the Union Territories. (राष्ट्रीय बहुआयामी गरीबी सूचकांक 2021 — पुदुचेरी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• India's first national MPI is based on the globally accepted methodology of the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) and UNDP.

• It uses three dimensions — Health, Education and Standard of Living — captured through 12 indicators.

• Among states, Bihar had the highest poverty; Kerala the lowest.

NOTE

• A person is "multidimensionally poor" if deprived in at least one-third (weighted) of the indicators.

question: Which Article of the Constitution of India specifically addresses the qualifications for the office of the President?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 58.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 58 of the Constitution lays down the qualifications for election as President of India. A candidate must:

◦ be a citizen of India;

◦ have completed 35 years of age;

◦ be qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha; and

◦ not hold any office of profit under the government.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Article 56 — term of office of the President (5 years).

• Article 60 — oath or affirmation by the President.

• Article 54 — election of the President (by an electoral college).

NOTE

• The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college through a system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.

question: Who among the following was the most important god of the Aryans?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Indra was the most important deity of the (Rig Vedic) Aryans. He was the god of thunder, rain and war, and the largest number of hymns in the Rigveda (about 250) are dedicated to him. (इंद्र — वर्षा एवं युद्ध के देवता)

• He is called "Purandara" — the destroyer of forts.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Agni (fire god) is second in importance, with about 200 hymns; he acted as an intermediary between gods and humans.

• Varuna was the upholder of the natural/moral order (Rita); Marut was the storm/wind god.

NOTE

• The Rig Vedic religion was naturalistic polytheism — worship of natural forces personified as gods, mainly through yajnas (sacrifices).

question: When was the All Bengal Students Conference held in the chairmanship of Jawaharlal Nehru?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1928.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The All Bengal Students Conference was held in 1928 under the chairmanship of Jawaharlal Nehru, reflecting his growing role in mobilising the youth of India during the freedom struggle. (अखिल बंगाल छात्र सम्मेलन — 1928)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The year 1928 also saw the Nehru Report, the visit of the Simon Commission and the Bardoli Satyagraha (led by Sardar Patel).

• Nehru, along with Subhas Chandra Bose, championed the demand for complete independence (Purna Swaraj).

NOTE

• The Purna Swaraj resolution was adopted at the Lahore Session (1929) under Nehru's presidency; 26 January 1930 was observed as the first Independence Day.

question: The autobiography of which of the following actors is titled 'The Substance And The Shadow: An Autobiography'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dilip Kumar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Dilip Kumar: The Substance and the Shadow – An Autobiography" is the life story of the legendary Hindi film actor Dilip Kumar (born Muhammad Yusuf Khan). (दिलीप कुमार की आत्मकथा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Dilip Kumar, called the "Tragedy King", was honoured with the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (1994) and the Padma Vibhushan (2015); Pakistan awarded him the Nishan-e-Imtiaz.

• His famous films include *Mughal-e-Azam*, *Devdas*, *Naya Daur* and *Ganga Jamuna*.

NOTE

• Other film autobiographies: *An Unsuitable Boy* (Karan Johar), *Khullam Khulla* (Rishi Kapoor), *The Kingdom of Rama* / *Romancing with Life* (Dev Anand).

question: What is the name of Formula E's first ever race in India, which was hosted in collaboration with the Telangana government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The 2023 Greenko Hyderabad E-Prix.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India's first-ever Formula E race was the 2023 Greenko Hyderabad E-Prix, held on 11 February 2023 on a street circuit around the Hussain Sagar Lake, in collaboration with the Telangana government. (ग्रीनको हैदराबाद ई-प्रिक्स)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Formula E is an all-electric single-seater motorsport championship, promoting sustainable e-mobility.

• The Hyderabad race was won by Jean-Éric Vergne (DS Penske).

NOTE

• Formula E cars are fully electric; the championship began in 2014 and is sanctioned by the FIA.

question: During which centuries did several Buddhist pilgrims and scholars travel to China on the historic 'silk route'?
option_1: First, second and third centuries AD
solution_text:
The correct answer is First, second and third centuries AD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• During the first, second and third centuries AD, several Buddhist monks, pilgrims and scholars travelled from India to China along the ancient Silk Route, carrying Buddhism and Indian culture to Central and East Asia. (रेशम मार्ग — पहली, दूसरी व तीसरी शताब्दी)

• This period coincided with the Kushana empire (notably Kanishka), a great patron of Buddhism.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Silk Route was a network of trade routes linking India, China, Central Asia and the Roman/Mediterranean world, used for silk, spices and ideas.

• The Mahayana form of Buddhism spread to China, Korea and Japan via this route.

NOTE

• Later Chinese travellers like Fa-Hien (5th c.) and Hiuen Tsang / Xuanzang (7th c.) came to India, but the outward spread to China was in the early centuries AD.

question: Non-polar molecules possess _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is instantaneous dipole moment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Non-polar molecules have no permanent dipole moment, but due to the momentary, random movement of electrons, a temporary uneven charge distribution can arise, giving them an instantaneous (temporary) dipole moment. (क्षणिक द्विध्रुव आघूर्ण)

• These instantaneous dipoles induce dipoles in neighbouring molecules, producing London dispersion forces (a type of van der Waals force).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• A permanent dipole moment (Option 1) is a feature of polar molecules such as H₂O and HCl, where there is a permanent separation of charge.

• Examples of non-polar molecules: O₂, N₂, CO₂, CH₄ and other symmetric molecules.

NOTE

• A molecule is non-polar if the bond dipoles cancel out due to symmetry (e.g., linear CO₂) or if it is made of identical atoms (e.g., O₂).

question: The Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) is an example of the _________ industry.
solution_text:
The correct answer is public sector.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) is a public sector undertaking, i.e. it is owned and managed by the Government of India. It is one of the largest steel producers in India. (सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र — सेल)

• SAIL is a Maharatna company.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• In the public sector, ownership and management lie with the government (e.g., SAIL, ONGC, BHEL, Indian Railways).

• In the private sector, they lie with private individuals/firms (e.g., TISCO/Tata Steel, Reliance).

• The joint sector involves both government and private participation; the cooperative sector is owned by members (e.g., Amul).

NOTE

• SAIL operates major integrated steel plants at Bhilai, Bokaro, Rourkela, Durgapur and Burnpur (IISCO).

question: Which Indian dancer of the Manipuri style won the Tagore Award for Cultural Harmony in 2014?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajkumar Singhajit Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rajkumar Singhajit Singh, an eminent exponent of the Manipuri classical dance style, was awarded the Tagore Award for Cultural Harmony for 2014. (मणिपुरी नृत्य — राजकुमार सिंहजीत सिंह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Tagore Award for Cultural Harmony was instituted in 2012 to commemorate the 150th birth anniversary of Rabindranath Tagore; the first awardee was Pandit Ravi Shankar.

• Manipuri is one of the eight classical dances, known for its graceful, gentle movements and themes of Radha–Krishna (Raslila).

NOTE

• The Tagore Award carries ₹1 crore, a citation, a plaque and an object of traditional handicraft/handloom.

question: Who among the following led the Parliamentary delegation to participate in the 9th BRICS Parliamentary Forum in September 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Harivansh Narayan Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Harivansh Narayan Singh, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, led the Indian Parliamentary delegation to the 9th BRICS Parliamentary Forum held in South Africa in September 2023. (हरिवंश नारायण सिंह — 9वाँ ब्रिक्स संसदीय मंच)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• BRICS originally comprised Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa; it was later expanded to include new members.

• The BRICS Parliamentary Forum promotes cooperation among the legislatures of member nations.

NOTE

• At the time, Jagdeep Dhankhar was the Vice-President/Rajya Sabha Chairman and Om Birla the Lok Sabha Speaker — common distractors here.

question: Which classical dance form is performed by the renowned artists; Sitara Devi, Rohini Bhate, Pandit Munnalal Shukla, Kumudini Lakhia and Uma Sharma?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sitara Devi, Rohini Bhate, Pandit Munnalal Shukla, Kumudini Lakhia and Uma Sharma are all celebrated exponents of the Kathak classical dance form of North India. (कथक)

• Kathak is known for fast footwork (tatkar), pirouettes (chakkars) and expressive storytelling (abhinaya).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sitara Devi was called the "Kathak Queen" and was praised by Rabindranath Tagore.

• Kumudini Lakhia and Birju Maharaj are other legendary names associated with Kathak.

NOTE

• Major gharanas of Kathak: Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras (and later Raigarh).

question: Select the synthetic indicator from among the given options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Methyl orange.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Methyl orange is a synthetic (man-made) acid–base indicator. It turns red in acidic solution and yellow in basic solution. (संश्लेषित सूचक — मिथाइल ऑरेंज)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Natural indicators: Litmus (from lichens), turmeric, red cabbage juice and china rose (hibiscus) — so options 1, 2 and 3 are natural indicators.

• Another common synthetic indicator is phenolphthalein (colourless in acid, pink in base).

NOTE

• Litmus turns red in acid and blue in base; turmeric turns red in base; methyl orange turns red in acid, yellow in base.

question: The Ramoshi Uprising of 1824 took place in which of the following present states of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ramoshi Uprising (from 1822–1824 onwards) took place in the Western Ghats region of present-day Maharashtra. The Ramoshis, a community that had served under the Maratha administration, revolted against British rule and economic hardship under leaders such as Chittur Singh and later Umaji Naik. (रामोसी विद्रोह — महाराष्ट्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The uprising was a form of tribal/peasant resistance to the loss of livelihood after the fall of the Maratha power in 1818.

• Umaji Naik is remembered as an early rebel against the British in Maharashtra.

NOTE

• Other tribal/peasant revolts: Santhal (1855–56), Munda/Ulgulan (Birsa Munda), Kol (1831) and Bhil uprisings.

question: In October 2023, Maharashtra government planned which of the following schemes to overhaul its medical system after the death of 38 patients in Nanded?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vision 2035.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In October 2023, following the deaths of patients at a government hospital in Nanded, the Maharashtra government announced a health-sector reform plan called "Vision 2035" to overhaul and strengthen its public medical system. (विज़न 2035 — महाराष्ट्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The plan aimed at upgrading hospital infrastructure, staffing, medicine supply and emergency care across the state.

NOTE

• "Sahakar Mitra" is a scheme related to cooperatives (NCDC); "Ayushman" is associated with the national Ayushman Bharat health scheme — used here as distractors.

question:
Which of the following options correctly matches column-A and column-B?

Column-A (Food component) — Column-B (Enzyme involved in digestion): i. Protein  a. Amylase  ii. Carbohydrates  b. Lipase  iii. Fats  c. Trypsin
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-c, ii-a, iii-b.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct matching of food components with their digestive enzymes is:

◦ i. Protein → c. Trypsin (a protease that digests proteins into peptides/amino acids).

◦ ii. Carbohydrates → a. Amylase (digests starch into maltose/sugars).

◦ iii. Fats → b. Lipase (digests fats into fatty acids and glycerol).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1 (i-c, ii-a, iii-b).

Additional Information

• Amylase is present in saliva (ptyalin) and pancreatic juice.

• Trypsin is secreted by the pancreas and acts in the small intestine (alkaline medium).

• Lipase (pancreatic) works with bile from the liver, which emulsifies fats.

NOTE

• Pepsin (in the stomach) also digests proteins in an acidic medium; bile does not contain enzymes but aids fat digestion.

question: A process like river bifurcation can create valuable landforms for the environment, providing growth of vegetation. An example of such landform is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is river deltas.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When a river bifurcates (splits into distributaries) near its mouth and deposits sediment, it forms a delta — a fertile, low-lying landform that supports rich vegetation and agriculture. (नदी डेल्टा)

◦ Example: The Sundarbans delta of the Ganga–Brahmaputra.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• A delta is a depositional landform formed in the lower course of a river.

• Potholes and V-shaped valleys are erosional landforms of the upper course; cascades are small waterfalls.

NOTE

• Major Indian deltas: Ganga–Brahmaputra (Sundarbans), Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri (Cauvery) and Mahanadi. The Godavari–Krishna–Kaveri form fertile "arcuate" deltas.

question: The Taj Mahal was built by who among the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shah Jahan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Taj Mahal at Agra was built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal (Arjumand Banu Begum). Construction began around 1632 and was completed around 1653. (ताजमहल — शाहजहाँ)

• It stands on the banks of the Yamuna river and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The chief architect is traditionally held to be Ustad Ahmad Lahauri.

• The Taj is a masterpiece of Mughal architecture, blending Persian, Islamic and Indian styles, built in white marble with pietra dura inlay.

NOTE

• Other monuments by Shah Jahan: the Red Fort and Jama Masjid (Delhi), and the Moti Masjid (Agra). His reign is called the "Golden Age" of Mughal architecture.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are FALSE for the Harappan town planning?

1. Most of the towns have citadel in harappan civilization.  2. Every town had a temple in Harappan civilization.  3. Every building was made of sand stone in Harappan civilization.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 2 and 3.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement 2 is FALSE: no clear temple has been identified in the Harappan (Indus Valley) civilization; unlike later civilizations, it had no monumental religious structures.

• Statement 3 is FALSE: Harappan buildings were made mainly of standardised, kiln-burnt (baked) bricks and mud bricks — not sandstone.

• Statement 1 is TRUE: most major towns (e.g., Harappa, Mohenjo-daro) had a raised citadel to the west and a lower town to the east.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4 (statements 2 and 3 are false).

Additional Information

• Harappan towns followed a grid pattern, with streets cutting at right angles and an advanced covered drainage system.

• The Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro is a notable structure on the citadel.

NOTE

• The uniform brick ratio (roughly 4:2:1) across sites shows remarkable standardisation in Harappan town planning.

question: __________ was the pioneer who modified the Hawaiian slide guitar to play classical ragas.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brij Bhushan Kabra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Brij Bhushan Kabra was the pioneering musician who adapted the Hawaiian slide guitar to play Indian classical ragas, establishing the guitar as a serious instrument in Hindustani classical music. (बृज भूषण काबरा — स्लाइड गिटार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• He was part of the famous fusion album "Call of the Valley" (1967) along with Pandit Shivkumar Sharma (santoor) and Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia (flute).

NOTE

• Buddhadev Dasgupta was a noted sarod player; Palghat Raghu was a Carnatic mridangam maestro — used here as distractors.

question: Which edition of the Intercontinental Cup event was played in India in 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3rd.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 2023 Intercontinental Cup (football) was the 3rd edition of the tournament, held in Bhubaneswar, India, in June 2023. India won the title, beating Lebanon in the final. (तीसरा इंटरकांटिनेंटल कप — 2023)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Intercontinental Cup is an international football tournament organised by the All India Football Federation (AIFF).

• India also won the inaugural 2018 edition (beating Kenya); the 2019 edition was won by North Korea.

NOTE

• India's captain Sunil Chhetri has been a key figure in these tournaments, and is among the highest international goal-scorers in football.

question: In the context of microfinance, what does 'S' stand for in SHG?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Self.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In microfinance, SHG stands for "Self Help Group". It is a small, voluntary association (usually of 10–20 people, often women) who pool their savings and provide small loans to members. (स्वयं सहायता समूह)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• SHGs are promoted under the SHG–Bank Linkage Programme launched by NABARD in 1992.

• They promote financial inclusion, women's empowerment and rural entrepreneurship, and are central to the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – NRLM.

NOTE

• Microfinance provides small-scale financial services to low-income groups who lack access to formal banking; SHGs are a key delivery channel in India.

question: In which state is 'Bhogali Bihu' festival celebrated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bhogali Bihu" (also called Magh Bihu) is a harvest festival of Assam, celebrated in mid-January (the month of Magh) to mark the end of the harvesting season, with feasting, bonfires (Meji) and community meals. (भोगाली बिहू — असम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Assam celebrates three Bihus: Rongali/Bohag Bihu (spring, April – the main New Year festival), Bhogali/Magh Bihu (January – harvest) and Kongali/Kati Bihu (autumn, October – austere).

NOTE

• Bhogali Bihu is a festival of food and feasting ("Bhog" = enjoyment/eating), featuring traditional cakes like pitha and laru.
